key_insight: LLM reasoning generalizes best when training traces can be decomposed into reusable atomic modules, with SFT providing compositional examples and RL discovering how to recombine them.
engineering_relevance: For reasoning systems, this suggests a two-stage training design: use SFT to cover core skills and trace structure, then use RL to explore and optimize novel compositions beyond the supervised support.
method: Formalize reasoning as a hierarchical latent selection model with discrete module-routing variables.
Treat reasoning traces as cascades of reusable atomic modules, including skills and selection/routing operations.
Analyze the asymmetric roles of SFT and RL in module provision versus module decomposition and recombination.
evidence_signal: Controlled experiments show RL can extract atomic modules from compound SFT traces and recombine them to solve unseen configurations, with compound-trace training outperforming isolated atomic-module training.
watch_item: The approach may depend on high-quality compositional traces and careful separation of SFT coverage from RL exploration, which could be difficult to achieve in large-scale real-world datasets.
paper_title: From Reasoning Traces to Reusable Modules: Understanding Compositional Generalization in Language Model Reasoning
